definitions.gloss: dawn of an era; early period; infancy
definitions.explanation: The very beginning or earliest stage of a field, movement, era, or technology. A formal and literary term often used in historical, academic, and journalistic writing.

examples.japanese: インターネットの{黎明期|れいめいき}を{知|し}っている。
examples.english: I remember the early days of the internet.

examples.japanese: {日本映画|にほんえいが}の{黎明期|れいめいき}について{研究|けんきゅう}している。
examples.english: I'm researching the dawn of Japanese cinema.

examples.japanese: AI{技術|ぎじゅつ}はまだ{黎明期|れいめいき}にあるが、すでに{社会|しゃかい}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}え{始|はじ}めている。
examples.english: AI technology is still in its infancy, but it has already begun to have a major impact on society.

notes:
Compound of {黎明|れいめい} (dawn, daybreak) + {期|き} (period). Literally the "dawn period" of something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黎明期|れいめいき}にある (be in the early stages)
- {黎明期|れいめいき}の{技術|ぎじゅつ} (early-stage technology)
- {黎明期|れいめいき}を{迎|むか}える (enter the dawn of)
- {黎明期|れいめいき}から (since the early days)

USAGE NOTES:
A formal, somewhat literary word. Common in essays, documentaries, and news features looking back at the origins of something. The standalone {黎明|れいめい} means dawn (literal or figurative) and can be used without {期|き} in more poetic contexts.
